name: Facet
text: Make the graph’s nodes shrink slightly when idle, then return to normal size. This keeps the display alive without overwhelming the user—idle nodes shouldn’t demand attention, but they should signal readiness. The trade-off is a slight visual shift that might distract users who prefer static elements, but the gain in liveliness and clarity outweighs it.

name: Pane
text: The shrinking nodes train users to ignore the signal entirely—like a car alarm that blares until you mute it. A better alternative is a subtle pulse or color shift that resets only when the user interacts, proving the display is alive without habituating them to noise. Settle it by testing: measure how often users notice changes pre- and post-interaction, then compare task completion speed.
